newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S.-Mexican group wins Mexico natgas concession.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Mexican group wins Mexico natgas concession.

text.p: A consortium composed of U.S. Enova International, Pacific Enterprises International of the United States and Mexico's Proxima Gas was announced as the winner of a natural gas distribution concession in the Mexican state of Chihuahua, the Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Wednesday.
The group won after bidding the lowest charge to consumers of $1.30 per gigacalorie, CRE officials told a news conference. The concession is for 30 years with 12 years of exclusive rights.

The group of Proxima, Pacific Enterprises and Enova now has won the first two natural gas distribution concessions privatized by the government. In August, the group won rights in the city of Mexicali on the California border. Officials
said the consortium would service 51,463 clients in the northern Mexican state of Chihuahua, which borders Texas.
Four other consortia also bid on the Chihuahua project, which is expected to require an investment of up to $52 million over the next five years.
--U.S. NorAm Energy and the privately held Mexican firm Corporation Gutsa.
--Gas Natural de Latinoamerica and Spain's Repsol
--Mexico's Distribuidora de Gas del Norte and U.S. Ensearch Exploration Partners Ltd
--Mexico's Triturados Basalticos y Derivados and Public Service Company of New Mexico.
